claim: Remark 5.3 of Bitar--Donoso--Petite, arXiv:2609.26479v1, is false for the paper's stated notion of strong double minimality unless an effectiveness hypothesis is added. Let \(G=\mathbb Z\times S_3\) and let \(\pi:G\to\mathbb Z\) be projection. Since \(Z(S_3)=\{e\}\), one has \(Z(G)=\mathbb Z\times\{e\}\) and hence \(\pi(Z(G))=\mathbb Z=Z(\mathbb Z)\). Take any strong doubly minimal \(\mathbb Z\)-system and pull it back along \(\pi\). Proposition 5.15 of the same paper proves that this pullback is again strong doubly minimal, while every element of \(\ker\pi\) acts trivially. But \(g=(0,(12))\) is noncentral and has finite conjugacy class, so \(g\in\operatorname{FC}(G)\setminus Z(G)\). Thus \(G\) admits a strong doubly minimal action despite \(\operatorname{FC}(G)\setminus Z(G)\ne\varnothing\), contradicting the group-level conclusion of Remark 5.3. The proof in Remark 5.3 fails here because the graph of \(S^g=\operatorname{id}\) is the diagonal, and Definition 5.1 imposes density only on pairs from different \(Z(G)\)-orbits. No claim is made against a faithful or effective-action version of the obstruction.
integrity: The counterexample is derived exactly from Definition 5.1 and Proposition 5.15 of the focal preprint plus elementary group facts about the center and conjugacy classes of \(S_3\). No numerical experiment or external certification is used.
scientific_limitations: The claim concerns the unconditional group-level conclusion of Remark 5.3 in arXiv:2609.26479v1; it does not refute a faithful-action variant.
No complete replacement criterion for the FC-center obstruction is proposed.
A later revision or unindexed correction could address the issue; none was located in the searches performed.
title: A nonfaithful pullback defeats an FC-center obstruction to strong double minimality
